question: How much do exact and near deduplication matter?

arms.change: Exact deduplication only; the baseline applies exact and near deduplication.

controls: P0 seed 1, the 50m baseline, is the shared baseline arm. Every arm trains experiments/ladder/50m at the learning rate the 50m learning-rate record selects, seed 1, from the same initial model tensors (verified by hash), with the same tokenizer, context, schedule and token budget. Only the named data change differs. Every arm is scored on the same validation packs: the baseline corpus's development-bucket families, held fixed across arms.
primary_metric: Mean final held-out loss over the fixed per-source validation packs, each source weighted equally; per-source losses reported alongside.
secondary_metrics: The pinned early-signal suite (scripts.open_slm_eval: HellaSwag, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, PIQA, ArithMark) on each arm's final export, and held-out loss at each quarter of the horizon.
minimum_useful_effect: 2.83 times the P0 standard deviation of the metric at 50m; an arm difference below it is reported as no detectable effect.
decision_rule: Keep near deduplication if exact-only is worse than the baseline by at least the minimum useful effect on the primary metric, and keep exact deduplication if no-dedup is worse than exact-only by the same margin. Report the cost per accepted token of each stage alongside.
data_preparation: Each arm reruns scripts.production_data_preprocess over the same inputs with only policy.deduplication changed (none or exact); the benchmark firewall and family partition apply unchanged in every arm. Each arm's ladder inputs bind the baseline preprocess's removal log per source as removals ({path, sha256}), so duplicates the baseline removed inherit their original's family bucket. The no-dedup arm's data configuration also sets dedup.scope to none, because packing otherwise removes exact copies itself.
prerequisites: The 50m baseline corpus is configured and P0 has run, so the minimum useful effect is known.
cost: Projected 0.9 GH200 GPU-hours per run (program design), or about 7.3 hours on the local RTX 3090 at its synthetic compiled rate of 100,000 tokens per second, before validation and saves.
